_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); net revenue, credit cost, expense, nonperforming-asset and pre-tax margin signals with JPMorgan Chase's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'JPMorgan Chase & Co. ... is a leading global financial services firm and one of the largest banking institutions in the United States' 'Our businesses have been, and in the future will continue to be, materially affected by economic and market conditions' 'There is increasing competition in the financial services industry which may adversely affect our results of operations.' (FY2009 10-K); DURABLE, risk 2: the 10-K ties results to markets and the economy, a cycle and a competitive field, and does not call its own business cyclical (the word does not appear in it: the LOW and SHW reading); no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a bank holding company on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

classification.quality_note: 'JPMorgan Chase & Co. ... is a leading global financial services firm and one of the largest banking institutions in the United States' 'Our businesses have been, and in the future will continue to be, materially affected by economic and market conditions' 'There is increasing competition in the financial services industry which may adversely affect our results of operations.' (FY2009 10-K); DURABLE, risk 2: the 10-K ties results to markets and the economy, a cycle and a competitive field, and does not call its own business cyclical (the word does not appear in it: the LOW and SHW reading); no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a bank holding company on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price fair; Ratio B 1.72x; +49% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.19; conservative 2yr -14%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -80.1%/yr (worst year FY03-FY09, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +0.6%/yr (Q1 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 7.4-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +0.6%/yr (FY03-FY09 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +63.4%/yr (best 2-yr run FY03-FY09, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: JPM (retrospective, 2010-06-11) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.72x (97.6% downside to Bear $0.92 / +56.7% upside to Bull $59.69) | Adj composite 2.43 vs market 2.24: gap +0.19 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +49% above the EPP floor $25.52 (11x FY10E $2.32) | Conservative 2-yr case: -13.6% total (-6.8%/yr) | At 16.4x FY10E the 15% hurdle price $50.37 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +10.6% YoY in Q1 2010, forward revenues +10.6% (Q1 2010 revenue growth (no Q2 2010 guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
